rationale: This is an additive stack of two well-documented anomalies (operating profitability à la Novy-Marx and net external financing à la Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan), and the SUMRANK average contradicts the stated "only scores high when both hold" conjunction logic, so it tests neither a new mechanism nor the interaction it claims.

The gating is internally consistent (unprofitable firms are pushed to the neutral middle of an industry z-score rather than mislabeled), and while net payout yield itself is published, conditioning it on sustained positive operating income is a defensible, testable refinement rather than a rediscovery.

Scaling net distributions by internally generated funds is a genuinely different denominator choice from the standard asset- or market-cap-scaled payout measures, but MAX(oancf, dp) can be arbitrarily close to zero for asset-light firms, so the cross-section may be driven by denominator noise even after 1% winsorization.

The core is the share-issuance anomaly (Pontiff-Woodgate / Daniel-Titman) with a profitability weight, and using raw GROWTH(csho) without split/stock-dividend adjustment injects large mechanical share-count changes that are unrelated to the market-timing hypothesis being tested.

Pairing a five-year profitability trend with contemporaneous leverage change is an economically coherent "internally financed improvement" story whose sign convention matches the expression, though the five-year TREND window will cut coverage and the two legs remain additive rather than truly interactive.

The first leg is simply the negative of total accruals (Sloan) and the second is net long-term debt issuance (Spiess-Affleck-Graves / Bradshaw et al.), so labelling the plain rank-average of two published anomalies as INTERACTION_TYPE "novel" overstates what is being tested.
